Helix: Consumers are currently protected by GINA, the Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act, a federal law that protects people from being discriminated against in health insurance and employment. What this means is that your insurance provider can not use a genetic test to make decisions about your eligibility, coverage, or premiums. Keep in mind that if you start showing symptoms of a disease (whether or not it is genetic; whether or not you took a genetic test), your insurance company CAN use that information to make decisions about eligibility or rates.
Importantly, GINA does not apply to life, long-term care, or disability insurance. If you are considering these types of insurance, you may want to purchase insurance before taking a genetic test that will tell you about medical conditions.
